inputs.share_count_basis: Actual shares outstanding at 30-Jun-2026 (294.8M, Q2-26 10-Q EPS note; the May-2026 ASR completed 10-Jun-2026 so no undelivered forward shares) plus 0.1M dilutive securities = 294.9M. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. withholding taxes on net-share settlement) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it. The 1:1 Mobility Global distribution did not change the SPGI share count.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow SBC add-back $236M consolidated, scaled to continuing operations (~$215M, ~1.6% of revenue); plus ~$100M/yr cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement (DB kpi equity_award_taxes FY2022 $110M / FY2023 $112M; FY2024-25 not separately tagged, inside the $148M H1-26 'employee withholding tax ... and other' financing line). Summed because SPGI publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure. Total ~2.3% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity 4.3% 10y UST + 1.0 beta x 5.0% ERP = 9.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.7% (5.0% pre-tax on the 2029-2036 curve, 25% tax); debt ~12% of capital at market (net debt $9.2B vs ~$114B equity) -> WACC ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. One WACC for all three scenarios: ratings-issuance cyclicality is charged in the bear flows, not in a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases: rent sits inside operating expense, hence inside the EBITDA margin (treatment A). Lease liabilities (~$0.44B non-current, continuing) are therefore NOT in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: CME Group owns 27% of S&P Dow Jones Indices (redeemable NCI, $4.9B carrying value at 31-Mar-2026). Charged ONCE, in the flows: the cash_tax_rate_path is a combined tax+NCI leakage driver (~22% cash tax + ~6% NCI share of EBIT, rising slightly as Indices outgrows the group). Not deducted again in the bridge. Calibration: FY2025 continuing-ops model NOPAT (13,589 x 49.9% x 0.72 = $4.88B) ties within ~1% to pro forma adjusted attributable NI $4,832M + after-tax interest $225M, once the 0.7pp one-off haircut and withholding taxes (not in NI) are added back.
inputs.net_debt_basis: 30-Jun-2026 10-Q, adjusted to post-spin: total debt $15,170M less the $1,981M (carrying) Mobility Global 2029/2031/2036 senior notes that became Mobility's sole obligation at separation = $13,189M (includes $825M commercial paper). Cash $4,134M less ~$121M estimated Mobility operating cash leaving with the spin (Mobility's cash in the 31-Mar-2026 pro forma balance sheet) = $4,013M; the $1.974B net cash distribution from Mobility stays with SPGI. Cross-check: 31-Mar-2026 Article 11 pro forma net debt $9,655M less ~$0.5B Q2 net cash generation after $0.5B ASR and dividends = ~$9.2B. Note the DB/CSV total_debt (16,015 at Q1-26) double-counts the current portion; the filing's own debt table is used. H2-2026 buybacks (~$5.5B remaining of the >$7B target) will raise net debt and lower the count after this date; both anchors are taken at 30-Jun-2026 so they are consistent.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (dcf-methods routing: operating company, asset-light recurring-revenue benchmarks/data business; first valuation of this ticker, no memory entry). SPIN-OFF DISCONTINUITY: Mobility (automotive data, ~$1.75B FY25 revenue, lower margin) was spun out as MBGL on 1-Jul-2026. The Metrics.csv history is the pre-spin consolidated company and is NOT extrapolated. FY0 is the 8-K/A (6-Jul-2026) Article 11 pro forma FY2025 continuing operations: revenue $13,589M, pro forma non-GAAP adjusted operating profit $6,974M (51.3%), adjusted diluted EPS $15.85. Year-1 (FY2026) is anchored to post-spin guidance (organic cc growth 6-8%, adj EPS $17.50-17.75) and H1-26 actuals (continuing revenue Q1 $3,717M + Q2 $3,678M = $7,395M, +10.8% on H1-25 pro forma $6,674M; Q1 adj op margin 52.9%, Q2 54.3%). MARGIN BUILD: FY26 adjusted op margin (post SBC expense, ex acquired-intangible amortization) ~52.5%, less a 0.7pp haircut because SPGI reports $300M+ of 'non-GAAP' restructuring/deal costs nearly every year (FY25: $341M ex amortization and disposal gains), plus SBC expense 1.6% and depreciation 0.8% => pre-SBC EBITDA 54.2%. Amortization of acquired intangibles ($766M continuing) is excluded from D&A: it is non-cash, largely non-deductible (IHS Markit was a stock merger) and has no capex counterpart. Capex (property + capitalized technology) ~1.1-1.2% of revenue. Working capital: unearned revenue (~$3.9B) slightly exceeds receivables growth, so a small positive 5% capture on the revenue change. BUYBACKS: SPGI is a heavy repurchaser ($5.0B FY25, >$7B FY26 target) so the flat count is funded, not a convention; buybacks are value-neutral in this model. Equity investments in unconsolidated subsidiaries ($605M) are left in the flows (their ~$28M equity income sits in operating profit), not added to the bridge. Accrued separation costs/taxes (~$156M in the pro forma) are not separately deducted (immaterial, ~$0.50/share). TIMING: the engine treats FY2026 as year 1, discounted a full period from FY0 (31-Dec-2025), while net debt is the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet that already contains H1-26 cash generation. The two roughly offset (H1-26 owner FCF counted twice, ~+$8/share; ~9 months of discounting not yet elapsed, ~-$20/share), so the value is if anything slightly conservative (~$10-15/share); no ad-hoc adjustment made.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Not the equity CAGR. Selected 7.5% = blend of the Nov-2025 Investor Day medium-term target (7-9% organic cc) and the FY2026 guide (6-8%), cross-checked against continuing-ops revenue CAGR FY2023-25 of 11.1% ($11,013M -> $13,589M, 8-K/A pro forma) which is flattered by a record issuance year.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is unusable: FY2022 IHS Markit all-stock merger lifted equity from $0.6B to $36.5B (5-yr CAGR meaningless, reported null), and ~$3-5B/yr of buybacks since then shrink book (-5.0% 3-yr) while revenue grew 11%. It diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs, as expected for a buyback compounder (same pattern as V). Revenue and FCF CAGRs over FY2020-25 are also inflated by the merger. Consolidated series include Mobility; they describe the pre-spin company.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the consolidated (pre-spin) Metrics.csv: revenue FY22 11,181 / FY20 7,442 -> FY25 15,336; EPS FY22 10.25 / FY20 9.71 -> FY25 14.67 (GAAP, deal amortization depresses it). Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes (FY24-25 taxes estimated at ~$110M): FY20 3,340, FY22 2,190 (depressed by IHS deal-related tax and cost payments), FY25 ~5,110. The 3-yr owner-FCF CAGR (32.6%) sits above the reported 29.5% because SBC grew slower than FCF from a depressed FY22 base; it is not a run-rate. No interest-income deduction: SPGI is net-debt.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 8%: H1 continuing revenue +10.8% but H2 laps a strong H2-25 and guidance is 6-8% organic; FY27 dips to 6.5% as the record 2025-26 refinancing/AI-capex issuance wave normalises, then 7% (inside the 7-9% medium-term target) gliding to 4% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: +40-50bp/yr early (below the 50-75bp/yr adjusted-margin target, since that target is pre-restructuring), flattening at ~56.7% pre-SBC EBITDA (~53.5% owner EBIT) by year 9.

bull.tax_rationale: NCI leakage rises faster in the bull because Indices (27% CME-owned) is the fastest grower.

scenario_narratives.base: Post-spin S&P Global compounds revenue at roughly its 7-9% medium-term target after a normal give-back from the 2025-26 issuance boom: Ratings grows mid-single-digit through the cycle with private-credit ratings (~25% growth) as the structural kicker, Indices compounds low-double-digit on passive AUM, Market Intelligence holds mid-single-digit subscription growth while AI is absorbed as a product feature (Spark Assist) rather than a substitute, and Energy/Platts grows mid-single-digit. Margins add 40-50bp a year as the simpler portfolio and scale leverage come through, with SPGI still spending ~$300M a year on 'non-recurring' restructuring. Capital return (>$7B FY26) keeps the count flat or falling.
scenario_narratives.bull: Three things go right together: (1) the 2027-28 leveraged-loan refinancing wall, AI/hyperscaler data-centre debt and private-credit ratings keep issuance-linked Ratings revenue near high-single-digit growth with no meaningful down-year; (2) Indices sustains mid-teens growth as passive share gains and private-markets/thematic indices broaden the franchise; (3) Market Intelligence uses proprietary data + GenAI to raise price and retention, so group margins reach ~58.5% pre-SBC EBITDA. Revenue growth runs 9%+ for five years and the market keeps paying ~22x terminal owner FCF for a duopoly benchmark franchise.
scenario_narratives.bear: Ratings is the largest and most cyclical segment and it is coming off record issuance. In the bear, a higher-for-longer rate shock or credit event in 2027 freezes issuance (2022 analogue: Ratings fell ~30%), taking group revenue flat for a year and compressing margins ~2pp on negative operating leverage; at the same time AI research tools steadily erode the desktop/research slice of Market Intelligence (~6-10% of revenue), capping recovery at 3-4.5% growth. Leverage taken on for buybacks limits flexibility; terminal value 18x on 2.5% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 20% because the largest segment is issuance-cyclical and the valuation date sits at record issuance after a strong H1, so a down-cycle within the forecast window is more likely than not at some point. Base 50% because the moat (NRSRO duopoly, S&P 500 licensing, Platts) makes the medium-term guide credible. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs Ratings, Indices and MI-AI monetisation to all go right at once. Result: price sits almost exactly on the base case (house basis); the market is paying the fully-SBC-expensed value for the base path, with no margin of safety against the 15% hurdle.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on the post-spin continuing business only. SBC plus withholding taxes are expensed and the share count held flat; the 27% CME stake in Indices is charged once as NCI leakage in the flows; net debt is the 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet adjusted for the Mobility notes that left with the spin. Historical consolidated CAGRs (IHS Markit merger, Mobility) are reported but not used to drive the projection; year 1 is anchored to the 8-K/A pro forma FY2025 and FY2026 guidance.
key_risks_to_valuation: Debt-issuance cyclicality: Ratings (~35% of revenue, ~65% margin) swings with rates and credit spreads; a 2022-style issuance freeze is the bear case
AI disintermediation of Market Intelligence research/desktop products
Terminal value carries most of the value at an 8.5% WACC; +/-1pp on WACC moves base value roughly 15-20%
Pro forma continuing-ops figures are preliminary until the Q3-2026 10-Q recasts history as discontinued operations
Regulatory risk to the issuer-pays ratings model and to index-provider concentration (low probability, high impact)
Net debt will rise through H2-2026 as the >$7B buyback is completed; the per-share value is unaffected only if repurchases happen below intrinsic value
